_comment: units.json — the canonical unit registry for auto nutrition (Phase 29a).
One entry per canonical unit; `spellings` are every accepted input form,
lowercase (matching is case-insensitive). `factor` is grams per 1 unit for
mass, millilitres per 1 unit for volume, and null for count — a count unit
resolves through food_portion, per food. The empty spelling "" is the
bare-count marker: an ingredient with a quantity and no unit ('2 eggs')
resolves through the 'each' portion.
`unresolvable` documents spellings the estimator deliberately skips — an
unknown spelling behaves identically, so this list is intent, not a gate.
Consumed by tool/nutrition.dart, which generates the food_unit table in
supabase/nutrition_foods.sql; the estimator (29c) reads that table, so this
file is the single source and nothing in SQL restates a conversion.
`display` (+ `plural` for word units) is the spelling an AUTHORED recipe
must use — the app prints `unit` verbatim, so this is what a cook reads.
It is NOT derivable from the key: `L` is displayed for key `l` (a lowercase
l reads as a 1), and word units keep a plural (`3 cloves`, never `3 clove`).
A unit with no `plural` is invariant at every quantity (`2 tbsp`). Read by
tool/recipe_format.dart's unit lint (BL-8), and since Phase 39 also emitted
into food_unit.display / .plural, where canonical_unit() in 0001 applies the
same canon to IMPORTED recipes (UX-030). The estimator never reads them. The
bare-count marker `each` has no display because an authored unit is null.
